lead: Original and editioned works of art a person owns, organised by medium (painting, works on paper, prints, photographs, sculpture, studio ceramics and glass, textile, calligraphy and paper art) with collectible figurines as their own department; artists sit in a ULAN-keyed artist register, artisan schools in the craft-traditions register, and period or movement is a view, not a kind.

b.v: unique original > artist-made edition > posthumous or interpretive edition > reproduction > restrike
b.w: Comes first; a work counts as original when made by the artist's hand or under the artist's direction.

b.v: signed and documented > attributed > circle/studio of > after/manner of
b.w: Auction-house attribution ladder; artist identity linked to Getty ULAN.

b.v: catalogue raisonné entry, exhibition history, certificate, gallery label
b.w: Facts about one work; shown as buying guidance.

b.v: cracks, fading, foxing, restoration, relining
b.w: Facts about the one work in hand, so shown as buying guidance only.
Judged against the artist's auction record; weighed after attribution.

depts.note: Kinds are media or painting traditions; artists go to the ULAN artist register; movements are a period view.

b.v: panel, canvas, paper, silk; original stretcher and ground
b.w: Identifies technique and age; relining and overpaint lower value.

b.v: antique, modern, contemporary
b.w: Looked at after original against reproduction.

s.brief: Variety by artist. Archetypes are named painting formats or genres that exist apart from one work (e.g. Old Master panel painting, plein-air oil sketch, colour-field canvas, street-art canvas), each with source; versions name reference artists with dates. Put notable artists (Old Masters, Impressionists, modern and contemporary blue chips, street artists such as Banksy, Shepard Fairey) in the brand register with seg 'Artist' and a Getty ULAN URL where retrieved. Spray-paint painting becomes 'Spray-paint and street-art painting'. Encaustic joins here (Jasper Johns, Fayum portraits as historic version). Supports (canvas, panel, board, paper) and genres (portrait, landscape, still life, abstract) go to 't'.

Archetypes: English watercolour school sketch (Turner, Cotman), botanical watercolour, gouache poster/illustration design; egg tempera icon-style panel and modern tempera (Andrew Wyeth); detached fresco fragment and strappo. Artists to the artist register with ULAN links. Keep definitions plain.

Chinese guohua and shan shui, Japanese sumi-e, Korean ink painting under Ink wash painting; mounting formats (hanging scroll/kakejiku, handscroll, album leaf, fan) as 't'. Nihonga archetypes and masters (Yokoyama Taikan, Higashiyama Kaii). Vietnamese sơn mài lacquer painting. New kinds: Painted folding screen (byōbu, Korean byeongpung; Kanō and Rinpa schools), Korean folk painting (minhwa: chaekgeori, tiger-and-magpie). Add tradition entries (Chinese literati painting, Kanō school, Rinpa, minhwa, sơn mài). Stress forgery risk in notes.

Portrait miniature: archetypes Tudor/Elizabethan limning (Hilliard), 18th-century ivory miniature, eye miniature; ivory legal note. New Persian and Indian miniature painting with archetypes per school (Persian/Safavid, Mughal, Rajput, Pahari, Deccani) and tradition entries. New Reverse glass painting (Hinterglasmalerei, Senegalese souwère, Chinese export reverse-glass). Icons and thangka are NOT kinds here (they stay in F4 as devotional panel and scroll paintings): add tradition entries for Orthodox icon painting and thangka painting with links to F4.

New kinds with sources and tradition entries: Aboriginal Australian painting (Western Desert dot painting, Papunya Tula; Arnhem Land bark painting; authenticity via art-centre certificates), Indian folk painting (Madhubani/Mithila, Pattachitra, Gond, Warli, Kalighat as archetypes), Tingatinga painting (Tanzania), Haitian and naive painting (Hector Hyppolite, Henri Rousseau as reference), Outsider art (art brut: Dubuffet's collection, Henry Darger, Adolf Wölfli; any medium), Mexican retablo and ex-voto painting. Artists to the artist register. Max ~8 kinds.

b.v: finished presentation drawing > preparatory study > sketchbook page
b.w: Auction practice for works on paper.

b.v: foxing, light-staining, trimming
b.w: Facts about one sheet.

s.brief: Kinds by medium. Archetypes: Old Master drawing (pen and wash, red chalk), academic figure study, architectural drawing, sketchbook. New kinds: Chalk drawing (sanguine, trois crayons), Metalpoint drawing (silverpoint). Ink-and-wash goes as a 't' of pen-and-ink. Artists to the artist register.

Production art collecting. Animation cel: archetypes Disney production cel (Courvoisier set-ups 1930s–40s), Warner Bros./Chuck Jones, Studio Ghibli cels, limited-edition sericel; types production cel, key set-up, sericel, drawing; versions by studio. New Original comic art (pencilled and inked pages, covers, splash pages; Heritage/ComicLink as market references; no title lists). New Illustration original (book, magazine and advertising art: Norman Rockwell, Golden Age illustrators). Studios and auction houses to the register only where useful.

depts.note: Organised by process; archetypes are landmark print series or portfolios, versions are editions and states.

b.v: unique, then limited, then open; small (under 50) before large
b.w: Comes first for prints.

b.m: Hand signature in pencil and numbering
b.w: Comes second.

b.v: lifetime impression > posthumous edition > restrike; early state before later
b.w: Catalogue raisonné practice for prints.

b.v: bon à tirer; artist's proof (capped at about 10 percent of the edition); hors commerce
b.w: Set by the College Art Association print guidelines.

b.v: certificate, chop mark, blind stamp, publisher's label
b.w: Facts about one edition.

s.brief: Archetypes are landmark series with editions as versions: Dürer engravings (Melencolia I, Knight Death and the Devil), Rembrandt etchings (Hundred Guilder Print; states), Goya Los Caprichos and Disasters of War (first edition 1799/1863 then later editions), Piranesi Carceri and Vedute di Roma, Whistler Thames Set, Hogarth series. Publishers/printers (e.g. Crown Point Press, Calcografía Nacional) to the register only if sourced.

Archetypes: Dürer Apocalypse woodcuts, German Expressionist woodcut (Die Brücke), Munch woodcuts, Picasso reduction linocuts, Thomas Bewick wood engravings, Gauguin Noa Noa. Japanese woodblock prints go to their own shelf. New kind Chinese New Year print (nianhua: Yangliuqing, Taohuawu, Weifang) with tradition entry.

Tradition entry for ukiyo-e (Edo publishers, carver/printer system, censor and publisher seals as authenticity markers; Watanabe reprints and later re-cuts as versions). New kinds with archetypes: Ukiyo-e print (Hokusai Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji incl. Great Wave; Hiroshige Fifty-three Stations of the Tōkaidō and One Hundred Famous Views of Edo; Utamaro bijin-ga; Sharaku actor prints), Shin-hanga (Watanabe Shōzaburō publisher; Kawase Hasui, Hiroshi Yoshida, Ito Shinsui), Sōsaku-hanga (Onchi Kōshirō, Munakata Shikō), Surimono. Types: formats ōban/chūban/triptych; genres bijin-ga, yakusha-e, fūkeiga.

Archetypes: Toulouse-Lautrec colour lithographs, Mourlot-printed lithographs (Picasso, Chagall, Miró), Tamarind and ULAE American lithography, Warhol screenprint portfolios (Marilyn 1967, Campbell's Soup I/II; Factory Additions and Sunday B. Morning as versions), Rauschenberg/Lichtenstein Gemini G.E.L. editions, Corita Kent, Banksy Pictures on Walls screenprints (POW edition, signed/unsigned). Lithograph keeps types Stone lithograph and Offset lithograph; add a plain definition and source. New kind Pochoir (Jean Saudé, Art Deco fashion plates).

Restraint plus a few archetypes with sources: Degas monotypes, Gauguin traced monotypes, Robert Rauschenberg/Jasper Johns embossed works, Tyler Graphics paper-pulp prints. Merge nothing; keep the monoprint/monotype distinction in definitions.

Mixed: variety for vintage posters, tier for reproductions. New Vintage poster: archetypes Belle Époque posters (Jules Chéret, Alphonse Mucha Gismonda, Toulouse-Lautrec Moulin Rouge), Art Deco travel posters (Cassandre Normandie, London Underground commissions), WPA posters, Swiss International Style; versions original lithograph vs later reprint; linen-backing as detail. New Exhibition and art poster (Mourlot exhibition posters, museum posters). Inkjet print becomes Giclée and fine-art reproduction (mark as reproduction). New Canvas and framed art print (QoL wall art: a few market-covering sellers only, e.g. IKEA, Desenio, King & McGaw, Society6 — sourced). Film posters as objects only, no title lists.

depts.note: Kinds are processes; photographers go to the artist register; snapshots, cartes de visite and cabinet cards stay in F5.

b.m: Process and print date against image date
b.v: vintage print > lifetime print > later or estate print
b.w: A print made near the time of the picture is called a vintage print.

b.v: unique, then limited, then open
b.w: Comes after process and date.

b.v: signed recto/verso, studio or agency stamp
b.w: Documents who printed it and when.

s.brief: Archetypes: Ansel Adams Museum Set / Special Edition prints (Moonrise, Hernandez), Magnum and Life-era press prints, Düsseldorf School large-format chromogenic prints (Gursky, Struth), Eggleston and Dye Transfer era, Cibachrome landscape prints; photographers to the artist register with ULAN where retrieved. Keep Ilfochrome as a version of silver dye bleach.

Processes 1839–1900s. Archetypes/versions: cased images (daguerreotype, ambrotype, tintype) with case types (leather, Union case) as 't'; makers Southworth & Hawes, Mathew Brady studio. New kinds: Salted paper print (Talbot calotype negatives), Albumen print (incl. travel and Civil War views), Photogravure (Camera Work, Edward Curtis The North American Indian), Autochrome (Lumière, 1907). Cartes de visite, cabinet cards and stereoviews stay in F5 (cross-link only).

Archetypes: Polaroid SX-70 and 20x24 camera works (Warhol, Walker Evans, Mapplethorpe), Steichen/Stieglitz platinum prints, Anna Atkins cyanotypes, Man Ray rayographs and Moholy-Nagy photograms. Instant print types: integral, peel-apart, Instax.

depts.note: Fine-art sculpture by material; mass-made figurines are their own department.

b.m: Cast or carved by the artist
b.v: unique carving > lifetime cast > posthumous authorised cast > surmoulage
b.w: Foundry and edition practice for bronzes.
Identifies authorised casts (e.g. Rudier, Susse, Valsuani).

s.brief: Archetypes: Rodin bronzes (The Thinker, editions by Rudier/Coubertin as versions), French animalier bronzes (Barye, Mêne), Art Deco chryselephantine figures (Chiparus, Preiss), Degas Little Dancer casts, Benin bronze heads (cultural-property note), Giacometti; terracotta maquettes and Tanagra figurines; plaster casts and gesso; wax models. Foundries to the register when sourced.

Archetypes: Carrara marble classical copies (Grand Tour), Volterra alabaster, Inuit soapstone carving (Cape Dorset/Kinngait; igloo tag as authenticity mark), Black Forest carving, Chinese jade (archaic bi disc, Qing boulder carving; nephrite vs jadeite), Japanese okimono, scrimshaw. New kind Netsuke (Japanese toggle carving; ivory, boxwood; signed carvers) with tradition entry. Ivory/CITES note on ivory and bone.

Traditional art as collected (Sotheby's/Christie's 'African, Oceanic and Pre-Columbian' categories). New kinds with tradition entries: African mask (Dan, Punu, Chokwe, Gelede; dance masks), African carved figure (Fang reliquary, Kongo nkisi, Baule, Yoruba ere ibeji, Dogon), Oceanic carving (Māori hei tiki, Asmat bis pole, Sepik), Pre-Columbian figure (Olmec, Colima, Moche). Authenticity: field-collected/used vs made-for-trade; provenance and cultural-property law notes.

Archetypes: welded steel (David Smith, Anthony Caro), Corten (Richard Serra), Calder mobiles and stabiles (new kind Mobile and kinetic sculpture: Calder, Tinguely, George Rickey), assemblage (Joseph Cornell boxes, Louise Nevelson), soft sculpture (Claes Oldenburg), neon (Tracey Emin, Bruce Nauman). Sculpture stand keeps kind-level, no archetypes, plain definition.

depts.note: Organised house → series → piece; resin pop-culture statues and designer toys stay in E1.

b.v: factory mark, date code, decorator's mark
b.w: Dates and authenticates a piece (e.g. Meissen crossed swords, Royal Doulton HN numbers, Hummel TMK trademarks).

b.v: limited edition > retired > current
b.w: Drives collector value.
Facts about one piece; shown as buying guidance.

s.brief: House → series → piece. Archetypes are series or named figures: Meissen (Kändler commedia dell'arte, Monkey Band), Royal Doulton HN figures (HN numbering; Pretty Ladies, The Old Balloon Seller HN1315) and character/Toby jugs, Lladró (keep its old figures as versions), M.I. Hummel by Goebel (TMK marks), Royal Copenhagen, Herend, Nymphenburg, Capodimonte, Gustavsberg (Malin), Precious Moments, Beswick animals, Royal Crown Derby paperweights. Cut the old flat SKU list: keep ≤5 versions per series with sources. New kinds: Staffordshire figure (flatbacks, Staffordshire dogs), Character and Toby jug (Royal Doulton, Ralph Wood). Earthenware/pottery is a 't' of the porcelain kind. House facts to the brand register.

New Crystal and glass figurine: take the Swarovski series from old k42 (Swarovski Crystal Society annual editions, Idyllia, Florere, Asian Symbols, Crystal Myriad, Signum) as archetypes with a few versions each; add Baccarat, Lalique, Daum crystal animals, Murano glass animals. Pewter and cast-metal figurine: Royal Selangor, Vienna cold-painted bronze (Bergmann), Britains-style figures only if not toy soldiers (toy soldiers stay in E1). Resin figurine becomes collectible resin figurine: Border Fine Arts, Willow Tree, Country Artists; pop-culture statues (Sideshow, Prime 1) belong to E1 and are cross-linked only.

depts.note: Signed artist and art-pottery works; production vases and decorative glass stay in B4, tableware in B5.

b.v: potter's seal or signature, studio mark, factory art-pottery mark
b.w: Identifies the maker and period.

b.m: Firing and glaze faults against intended effects
b.w: Kiln cracks and repairs lower value; intentional crawl or ash glaze do not.

s.brief: New kinds with archetypes and artists in the register: Studio pottery vessel (Bernard Leach, Shoji Hamada, Lucie Rie, Hans Coper, Peter Voulkos, Magdalene Odundo; Leach Pottery standard ware as archetype), Ceramic sculpture (Voulkos, Grayson Perry vases, contemporary), Art pottery (Moorcroft, Rookwood, Grueby, Martin Brothers, Clarice Cliff Bizarre, Wedgwood Fairyland Lustre), Asian art ceramics (Chinese imperial porcelain by reign mark, celadon, Japanese Raku, Bizen, Imari/Kakiemon, Satsuma, Korean moon jar). Tradition entries: mingei, Raku, Bizen, Jingdezhen porcelain, Korean celadon. Exclude dinnerware (B5) and decor vases (B4).

New kinds: Studio glass (American Studio Glass movement: Harvey Littleton, Dale Chihuly Macchia/Persians, Lino Tagliapietra, Toots Zynsky), Art glass (Tiffany Favrile, Émile Gallé and Daum cameo glass, Loetz, Lalique pâte-de-verre, Steuben Aurene, Venini/Murano studio pieces with archetypes Fazzoletto only as cross-link to B4), Stained-glass panel (leaded autonomous panels, Tiffany windows, Harry Clarke). Tradition entries: Murano, Nancy School (École de Nancy), Studio Glass movement. Tiffany lamps stay in B3.

b.v: hand-woven or hand-stitched > Jacquard or machine embroidery
b.w: Main authenticity question for textile art.

b.v: fading, moth, losses, old repairs
b.w: Facts about one piece.

s.brief: Tapestry archetypes: Aubusson, Gobelins, Flemish verdure, Arts & Crafts Morris & Co. Merton Abbey, modern artist tapestries (Lurçat, Dovecot Studios). Embroidered picture: stumpwork, Berlin woolwork, silk-work picture, Chinese Suzhou embroidery. New kinds: Needlework sampler (alphabet and band samplers, dated, schoolgirl samplers), Art quilt (Gee's Bend, Studio Art Quilt movement; bed quilts stay in B2), Appliqué textile picture (Kuna mola, Chilean arpillera, Fon appliqué of Benin, Hmong story cloth). Tradition entries for each.

b.v: signed and sealed by the calligrapher > workshop > print reproduction
b.w: Seals and signatures authenticate East Asian and Islamic calligraphy.

s.brief: Calligraphy splits by tradition. East Asian calligraphy (shufa/shodō/seoye): scripts seal, clerical, regular, running, cursive as 't'; formats hanging scroll, couplet, handscroll; masters to the artist register. New Islamic calligraphy: archetypes hilye, qit'a, levha, tughra, calligraphic panel; Ottoman hattat masters (Hafız Osman); tradition entry. New Western calligraphy (lettering art, broadsides; Edward Johnston). Illuminated manuscripts stay in F1. Carved seal: archetypes Shoushan and Qingtian stone seals, seal-carving schools (Xiling Seal Engravers' Society) as tradition.

Archetypes: Cubist papier collé (Picasso, Braque), Matisse cut-outs, Kurt Schwitters Merz; Roman and Byzantine mosaic fragments, micromosaic (Vatican mosaic studio, Grand Tour souvenirs); paper cut traditions jianzhi, Scherenschnitte, kirie, Polish wycinanki, Mexican papel picado with tradition entries. New kind Silhouette portrait (cut or painted profile; Auguste Edouart, 18th–19th century).
